preamble: Diphthongization of stressed [a] to [ie] after a palatal or palatalized consonant is Bartsch's law, a 5th-6th century change of northern Gallo-Romance: Latin a in stressed open syllables preceded by a palatalized velar (and some other palatal contexts) became Old French ie, as in cārum > chier and canem > chien. Outside this Gallo-Romance law, a direct a > ie shift is rare; the better-known Romance ie diphthongs (Spanish piedra, tierra) come from Latin short e, not a.

examples.note: Stressed open-syllable a after the palatalized velar (Latin k > tʃ before a) became ie by Bartsch's law; modern French cher [ʃɛʁ] later reduced the diphthong.
Same conditioning; the ie diphthong survives in modern French chien [ʃjɛ̃].
Source of English chief; modern French chef.
